meta.note: APPEND-ONLY additions that exercise the hardened identity stack (civ-2 identity + lineage + migration + compatibility) per Increment 5 plan §1. The accepted corpus is read verbatim and unchanged. Unlike the accepted corpus (shaped for the line-aware v1.0 classifier), these cases carry STABLE contextAnchors because civ-2 is line-blind by design and distinguishes co-located occurrences only by stable structural context. Synthetic, ground-truth-labelled, deterministic. Evidence only — not a baseline.

cases.name: add-classification-independence
cases.justification: §1 classification-independence: civ-2 derives identity from rule+subject+location+contextAnchor and EXCLUDES classification/role; the same review item keeps its id whether it is classified new or existing.

cases.name: add-verified-rename-continuity
cases.justification: §1 verified rename continuity: identity is preserved across a repo-metadata verified rename (filename change alone, same rule/subject/context).

cases.name: add-ambiguous-competing-rename
cases.justification: §1 ambiguous reopen / competing rename: two verified-rename predecessors resolve to the same target → lineage is not invented → ambiguous by design.

cases.name: add-reintroduction-reopened
cases.justification: §1 reintroduction: a deterministic identity match to a RESOLVED predecessor (same rule/subject/location/context) reopens the candidate → reintroduced (real drift), never silently the same.

cases.name: add-split-new-occurrence
cases.justification: §1 split → migration oneToMany: one existing candidate plus a NEW occurrence at the same rule/subject/location under a different stable context → split; the new occurrence is real drift and must be surfaced.

cases.name: add-indistinguishable-duplicates
cases.justification: §1 indistinguishable duplicates: two occurrences with identical rule/subject/location and NO distinguishing context → ambiguous by design; civ-2 never fabricates a stable ordinal.

cases.name: add-candidate-identity-version-suspension
cases.justification: §1 incompatible identity-version suspension: an accepted candidateIdentityVersion (civ-2) vs a current civ-1 is an identity-version incompatibility → evaluation SUSPENDS before any classification (Increment-2 contract now covers candidateIdentityVersion).

migration.note: civ-1 → proposed civ-2 migration scenario exercising all five mapping classifications (§1 split/merge; ambiguity preserved; every old candidate visible). oldIds are civ-1 placeholders (authoritative ids are never altered); linkage + lineageStatus are CONSUMED, never inferred here.
